statement: The room calls its own members, and kindred subs, to come and place for a work: to start it, build it, finish it or hold it.
range: from one unanswered post asking who will help to a run of calls, cheering and a set time for placing together

statement: The room settles what its mark will show of it: a member proposes a picture, the room argues its design, makes its land's flag or emblems the mark, signs it or leaves it unsigned, claims a mark others made, adds to it or enlarges it, or adds a personal piece to a shared mark.
range: from a single member's unanswered proposal to a design argued over days and redone, or a nation's flag sized and filled with its emblems, or one member asking to add their own words to a shared flag

statement: The room builds its mark, and members report its state to the thread: what is placed, done or missing, and where.
range: from one report that the logo is half done to reports on each part of a mark over two days

statement: Members circulate a template that lays out the mark pixel by pixel, or coordinates that locate it, ask for them, and ask strays to keep to them.
range: from one anchor coordinate to an official template the room asks everyone to follow against other versions

statement: The room keeps its placed work against erosion: members watch it and repair changed pixels, and the room rallies to defend it under attack, covers the night, hardens its shape and puts upkeep before growth. Repair restores the form the keepers know. A change the room has planned or agreed (P02) is therefore repaired away as damage until its keepers are told of it, and it is lost or given up where the telling does not reach them.
range: from one member fixing stray pixels to shifts, scripts and calls to defend over many hours

statement: Members work out who changed their work and why: they trace placers and rooms, find friendly fire or their own mistake, blame officers, or disown placers acting in their name.
range: from one question who keeps adding a line to a dossier on a rival's bots
cut_cost: P06 stated that members work out who changed their work and why (Attribution, 155 rooms); the model can no longer say that this step is part of organizing, and keeps only that it was tested as the step between restraint and attack and not found; its acts are mostly blaming and wondering, which hold no coordinating turn under the A1 rule

statement: Rooms spare their neighbours' work, rein in their own attackers, apologise for damage and appeal to attackers to stop.
range: from one member refusing to cover a neighbour to a room restoring a work it had damaged

statement: Rooms propose, settle and contest borders, truces and deals with neighbours by talk, through envoys, and hold each other to them.
range: from a one-line border agreed in a thread to treaties across languages kept and broken over a day

statement: Rooms attack others' work by the recurring moves the canvas affords: erasing, encroaching, converting a sign, raiding on a streamer's call, planting a script, altering a work as a joke.
range: from one member's call to deface a rival to a coordinated raid

statement: After the work is erased or overrun, the room weighs fighting for the spot against moving, and moves: a new spot, a smaller version, a fresh start.
range: from a lone member asking where to rebuild to a room relocating together within two hours

statement: When a work is up, the room marks it: announces it, celebrates it, credits makers and helpers, reports members' own parts and says what working with strangers meant.
range: from one 'We did it!' post to threads of credit and reflection at the close

statement: The room records what happened to its work and to the canvas around it: screenshots and timelapses, reports of its fate, mourning, imagined art, atlas entries, the end marked.
range: from one screenshot request to a full account of the week

statement: Near the close and after it, the room decides what of its temporary effort to keep: a later canvas, a new purpose for its canvas sub, the mark in its banner, ties with other rooms, the work remade elsewhere.
range: from a wish to do better next year to a canvas-born collective announcing a group to carry on

statement: Members add placements with scripts, bots and spare accounts, and the room argues over these machine hands and adjusts them.
range: from one member running spare accounts to a shared bot holding several rooms' works

statement: A member answers a call or proposal in one line that joins, assents, reports a part done or thanks, and the line asks for nothing back.
range: from 'On it.' to 'Did my part.'

statement: The host sub is keyed as play for April Fools: members post fakes and takeovers under the one-day licence, and a claim in it, a call to the canvas included, may be a joke.
range: from one fake post in an ordinary sub to a sub given over to parody for a day and a half
cut_cost: K01 stated that the host sub is keyed as play for April Fools (Keying, 368 rooms); the model can no longer name the frame the odd room ran inside, and keeps F-009, that the frame did not delay the canvas work across rooms; April Fools talk holds no coordinating turn under the A1 rule
restored_why: the criterion written before pass 1 ranks the story rooms told without a residue above the number of elements; the April Fools frame is told through K01, beside the work, in 10 of the 16 pass 5 story rooms told with no residue (ubc, ultrahardcore, CKCrusaders, cardinals, completeanarchy, lakers, rpi, unitedkingdom, NieR, bannedfromanime_irl); with K01 out of the model, the frame in those rooms would be residue, as Visibility returns was at C2; the cut is reversed. K01 still carries no arrow; it stands as a condition that the work ran beside (F-009)

statement: The room judges that it has too few hands or too little room for the work it wants: doubt, a canvas judged too full, a work judged absent or outclassed.
range: from one member saying there are not enough people to defenders told to give up

statement: Most rooms worked on their marks without deciding how they were organized: a decided element of order (a leader, a vote, an oath, a sanction, a division of the work) is coded in 46 of 705 rooms (F-006).
range: from rooms that say they wing it to colour factions holding elections

statement: The starter: a member who proposes the mark, maps it or begins placing it. Others joining is not part of the role: it is the answer to the room's call (P15), in the order A02 and A01 state.
range: from a member who only asks to a member who maps and places alone first

statement: The envoy: a member who acts for a room toward another room, carrying a proposal between threads or chats.
range: from a member calling themself a diplomat once to a standing representative in a shared council
cut_cost: R02 named the envoy, a member who acts for a room toward another room (13 rooms); the model can no longer name the role; P08 still holds settling deals through envoys, since its fourth-order theme Negotiated order holds the envoys' theme

statement: Rooms help one another's works and trade help: they give pixels to a neighbour's mark, ask other rooms for help, barter help for space or repair, thank their allies, greet them, and turn requests away.
range: from one member placing a pixel on a neighbour's flag to rooms trading night-time repairs for room on their mark

statement: Rooms join other rooms in coalitions: they meet in shared chats, form alliances, gather kindred rooms in a hub, tally kindred rooms' works and make joint marks.
range: from two rooms agreeing to defend each other to a council of kindred rooms holding a stretch of the canvas together

statement: Rooms carry a contest with a rival room in talk: they trade taunts, flood the rival's threads, claim victory, salute the rival after the fight and blame attackers after the close.
range: from one taunt in a thread to days of chants, victory claims and an after-the-fight salute

statement: The community carries a quarrel from before the canvas into it: a rival sub, a sports or national rivalry, an old dispute.
range: from one member naming the sub's old rival to a room whose first canvas act is against that rival

statement: The host sub draws a line around canvas talk: moderators gather it into a megathread, remove canvas posts by rule, change posting rules, pause the sub's usual events or disown the work; members open a canvas sub, object to the flood or argue the canvas's worth.
range: from one member asking for a megathread to moderators moving all canvas talk to a new sub and removing the rest

statement: The room acts as a body it was before the canvas, or as a faith in a colour: it argues the nation's history, belonging and politics beyond its flag, carries in the sub's quarrel, lore, jokes or ideology, or professes and spreads a colour.
range: from a fandom's running joke in canvas talk to a canvas fight told as the nation's history

statement: One room's work lives on another room's mark or territory under the host's rule: guests ask for space or protection, hosts rule on requests, and both sides dispute who may approve.
range: from a small room asking to slip into a neighbour's lot to a flag hosting dozens of works by application and vote

statement: In some rooms, a tie the room had before the canvas (a league or school rivalry, a nation's history, an ideology, lore) names the rival in the same turn that calls for or carries out the attack.
range: from a team's colours turned on a league rival's logo to a war from the nation's history named as the reason to cover a neighbour's flag

statement: Members dispute, or state the limits of, who may commit the room to an agreement with other rooms: they say that one member's agreement does not bind every placer, deny that a treaty speaks for them, or ask another group for a leader to deal with.
range: from one member saying that a deal cannot stop everyone to a treaty announced in r/place answered 'You don't speak for me, man.'
level: between rooms; a room shows its side in its own members' talk
field_mark: firm: the disclaimers, the denial and the request for a group leader are public exchanges; provisional: that an agreement or coalition prompts the dispute

statement: After placement ends, members contest which version of the canvas and of the event is kept: they ask a cleanup of a shared copy to fix their work, take part in it, argue that the cleanup should keep the damage as history, and correct accounts of the event that describe their group wrongly.
range: from one member correcting a claim about the room's work, or asking that a logo be cleaned in a shared copy, to a room arguing that its scars are its history
level: the event (a shared copy and public histories of the whole canvas); a room shows its side in its own members' talk after hour 73

evidence.note: room items found by a keyword search after hour 73 (c4_grep_hours.py), not by a theme; no third-order theme carries this yet

field_mark: firm: the sector instructions, the question of who decides, the retention decision, the objection to sterilising history and the correction promised are public exchanges; provisional: that preserving a shared object requires negotiating its legitimate version; the execution of the cleanup is not observed
